text:
maddie: quick idea — i sketched a lightweight closure rhythm for postmortems. short version: three checkpoints (T+24h, T+72h, T+30d) + an owner passport so handoffs are explicit. want quick thumbs before i put this in the runbook. :eyes:

raj: love the cadence. can we add a small SLA for action owners (e.g., acknowledge in 24h, plan in 72h)? otherwise hard to track.

lina: +1. ops-bot reminders for each checkpoint would help. also suggest we tag recurring patterns at T+72 so we can route to pattern leads.

sam: fwiw, the last incident we had the followups evaporated after handoff. strongly +1 for an owner passport (fields: owner, backup, acceptance criteria, due).

maddie: exactly. thinking a minimal passport copied into the issue so it's portable. example fields below — super tiny snippet: 
```
owner: @name
backup: @name
due: 2026-04-15 (T+72)
acceptance: perf regressed <2% for 7d or revert rolled out
pattern: cache-warmup
```

jordan: rotation note: can we make IC rotation monthly and have a secondary IC as standard? that reduces burnout and gives incoming IC a buddy for handoffs.

raj: monthly makes sense. also recommend a lightweight checklist for incoming IC: 1) open followup card, 2) confirm owners, 3) schedule T+72 sync.

lina: ops-bot can emit that checklist automatically when an incident is closed. i can add a small webhook.

ops-bot: scheduled: create followup card for INC-2026-0421 at 2026-04-14T10:00Z (T+24). reminder DM to owner at T+24 and T+72.

maddie: thanks. two more proposals: (1) a "recurrence" label we attach if the postmortem tags a pattern seen >2 times in 90 days, and (2) a short quarterly "pattern grooming" slot owned by platform to triage pattern leads.

sam: +1 to recurrence label. can we also add a tiny metric: % of actions with owners closed by due date? helps measure followthrough.

maddie: good metric idea. i'll add a column in the tracker and a tiny dashboard tile.

jordan: one last operational ask — please include comms cadence in the template: who updates customers, who owns internal comms, and a simple 3-line status template. avoiding ad-hoc messages keeps ops calm.

maddie: will do. i'll draft the runbook update and PR the template tomorrow. tagging folks for review: @raj @lina @sam @jordan. thanks for quick feedback. :thumbsup:
